prompt: Simplify: $x^3 \cdot x^4$. Write your answer as a power of $x$.
hint: $x^3$ is 3 copies of $x$, and $x^4$ is 4 more copies. Count ALL the copies.

hints.text: $x^3$ is 3 copies of $x$, and $x^4$ is 4 more copies. Count ALL the copies.
Multiplying powers with the same base ADDS the exponents: $x^{3+4}$.

explanation: $x^3 \cdot x^4$ means $(x \cdot x \cdot x)(x \cdot x \cdot x \cdot x)$ — copies of $x$ lined up.
So $x^3 \cdot x^4 = x^7$. Product rule: add the exponents.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with real numbers
steps: 128 is 2⁷, not 2¹². So the exponents add: x⁷.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two boxes of copies
steps: Picture a box holding 3 x-tiles and a box holding 4 x-tiles, all being multiplied together.
Dump both boxes into one: 3 + 4 = 7 tiles, which is x⁷.
